Results.ReviewText: I've grilled a variety of items now on my Spirit II E-310, and I am very satisfied. The thermometer is not as accurate as I would like, but that seems to be true with most grills. It does hold the temp well, and gets up to temp pretty fast. This grill is big enough for good indirect cooking, and does a great job with high heat for searing. When trying to get high heat I recommend starting with one burner at a time, and letting it run for a minute or two before lighting the next. It seems that lighting them all one right after the other causes the regulator, or gas flow from some other area, to cause a weak flow in all burners. I really like the construction of this grill, as it seems like it will last me a lot longer than the cheaper ones I've bought in the past. And you can't beat the warranty!

Results.ReviewText:
Overall I'm really happy with the grill and I think you're getting what is probably the best Value/Price ratio out there. The Ten-Year Guarantee was what clinched the deal for me.

One Star Off for Shipping: It arrived with a crack in the a cast aluminum grill box; essentially the largest and probably most expensive part. It was clearly a shipping issue and why they skimped on the packing around such a large/expensive product, I can't say. Weber was great about immediately honoring the warranted however so that's a plus (and the new grill-box was sent in much better packaging). It took almost a month to actually arrive though, which was definitely a little annoying. In the end it all worked out though and is now good to go.

ASSEMBLY REVIEW: This is the type of project that, if you like building things and are a regular DIY type of person, it will be all pretty straight forward. For me, it was sort of fun, and I'd rather see how it all is built than have it just "show up." If this is not you, then it'd be best to pay the extra for assembly I guess, or get a friend who's "mechanical" to help. I think it took maybe 2-3 hours overall and I really took my time with it. It's packed together really densely and that sort of slows things down. AGAIN: With some much packed in there, they really need another layer at least around the outside to better protect it. Anyway,I unpacked ALL of it first and I suggest you do that too. I made sure to have each section all laid out on a swept garage floor and sets of screws next to them.

INSTRUCTIONS: Mostly pretty well written and illustrated. Certain sections were lacking in explanations; others gave more info than needed. Some of the guidance is frankly crazy though, like the admonition to "not" use a powered drill/screw-driver for for the several dozen screws! Seriously? Just set your drill to a low torque setting so nothing gets stripped out; otherwise plan to add at least an additional hour or more for the build. Also, they say you'll need two people to do it, which I really can't see why. No section is all that heavy, nor anything truly needing more than two hands.

ACTUAL ASSEMBLY AND BUILD: For the most part I was pretty happy with the way it came together, and I could see that some decent engineering when into it. Having heavy coated screws is a good idea so you won't be getting any rust at those points. Some of the structure is not as heavy as I'd liked, but I'll grant that once all put together, the structure overall is pretty well tied together and should be relatively strong. 

Areas that are important for durability definitely are well-made: the grill box is heavy cast aluminum, and that's the section that normally would rust out (all my previous grills did, and I'm sure yours have too). I've had heavy cast aluminum pots and pans before and basically the never wear out no matter how times they get used or cooked with, so that's what I expect with this too. The grill "grids" (the portion you actually grill on) are really heavy duty cast iron parts and I also expect these to last at least the decade that they are guaranteed for. The KNOBS I am not a huge fan of, being plastic and probably the type of part that might wear just from weather  or age; we'll see.

Once I was done assembly I "cooked it in" for about 45 minutes (meaning I fired up all three zones at high and just let it go without any food inside). It definitely had some (but not a lot) leftover manufacturing oils or cleaners on some surfaces, so you want to burn all that off first. I put in a little foil bowl of wood cooking chips to get some smoked flavor to coat the inner surfaces too. It probably was a few days before it got to a more optimal "flavor" which is just like any new cook pan.

USAGE and FEATURES: I'll state upfront that the idea of this being "app connected" is absolutely ridiculous to me, and counter to the reason for getting outside and grilling in the first place. And even if I did use it, I have a hard time believing the electronics it uses will last more than year or so, especially once it goes through a few hard winters. I always cover the grill after each usage, but that won't do much for a weeks of below freezing temps that we get in New England.
The integrated Fuel Tank Scale is genius and such a simple but useful feature. I usually have a spare gas tank on-hand but in the past there have been a few occasions when the fuel ran out unexpectedly and that's never fun when you food is half-way cooked. This will at least give me a heads-up when things are getting low.

GRILLING/COOKING: After having this for around two months and using it on average 3-5 times a week I have to say, it works great. I get consistent, great tasting burgers, steaks, pork-loin and veggies out of it every time. It heats up really quickly, but I have yet to have anything burn at all. The cast iron grill grids are excellent, and the thermometer in the lid seems repetitively accurate (I'm not looking for anything exact, just a decent idea). Super easy to keep clean the inside and the outside for the most part as well. I use a little spay oil on the stainless steel sections for cleaning and polishing, figuring that I don't want to keep putting steel chemical polish on it all the time. Otherwise, get yourself a grill cover and you'll be good to go.
Results.Title: Well Designed Grill, Good Value for the Price

Results.ReviewText: Purchased last month through major home repair retailer and when received, main support/legs were bent. Called Weber customer support and the person I spoke to was outstanding. She was very knowledgeable and very courteous; even found out her training involved building the grill she was supporting--very impressive. She sent new support leg the next day and when received, had the grill built in three hours. When building it, you could tell it was quality made and was made for many years of trouble free grilling. Have grilled several meals and all perfect! The reason I purchased the grill in the first place is during a past party where I needed to feed many people, I had my grill made by another manufacturer and borrowed a relatives grill which was a Weber that was over 10 years old (relative actually commented on how he can still get parts for his Weber when needed). Had many compliments on the food that came from the old Weber grill. I could tell the difference which I attributed to the engineering of the Weber, how there is minimum flare ups and even heating throughout the cooking area. Would not buy another manufacturer's grill after this one. Although, with the 10 year warranty, I won't need to for a very long time!

Results.ReviewText: I bought this grill to replace my beloved Genesis, which I gave to my adult daughter. As an empty nester, the Spirit II is a better size for me. It is a Weber through and through, and is the 8th Weber I have owned, gas and charcoal. I have only owned Webers. Overall the Spirit II performs beautifully and predictably. I do experience some heat variations side to side, but all grills have that, and I simply have to learn the heat pattern. The one other observation is that when the left shelf is in the folded-down position, rain water will accumulate in the plastic shelf end-cap where the venturi cleaner is stored. The accumulated water splashes out unexpectedly when I lift the shelf into position. A minor matter, for sure, and a couple of holes drilled into the end cap will fix it. Overall, a really nice grill to cook on, direct and indirect. Predictable, reliable, easy to operate, and a great value. I know I will love having it right outside the kitchen door in the winter!
Results.Title: Everything I was looking for
